entries.error_pattern: CREATE POLICY IF NOT EXISTS ... syntax error at or near NOT
error_symptoms: supabase db push fails on a CREATE POLICY line
auto-generated RLS migration won t apply
migration valid except the policy statements

solution.approach: Postgres has NO IF NOT EXISTS on CREATE POLICY. Guard it in a DO block checking pg_policies (idempotent + valid). CREATE TABLE/INDEX + ALTER ENABLE RLS DO support idempotent forms — only CREATE POLICY does not.
solution.answer: Replace CREATE POLICY IF NOT EXISTS "name" ON tbl ... with: DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_policies WHERE schemaname=^public^ AND tablename=^tbl^ AND policyname=^name^) THEN CREATE POLICY "name" ON tbl ...; END IF; END $$;  (or DROP POLICY IF EXISTS then CREATE).

entries.error_pattern: The naive-tester survey returns a DIFFERENT verdict on the SAME product across runs (score and PRE-HARD judgments vary run-to-run)
error_symptoms: deal-findrs run A: 13/14, P3 FAIL (two-audience landing judged incoherent)
deal-findrs run B (same site, same commit): 12/14, P3 PASS (same two-audience landing judged a coherent distributor model)
the set of 'unevidenced' fields also shifts between runs (run B flagged both Prospect type AND ICP buyer title; run A flagged Prospect type only)
verdict can flip RENOVATION/TEARDOWN-adjacent on borderline products purely from run variance

CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-06-03: same deal-findrs site/commit scored 13/14, then 12/14 RENOVATION, then 10/14 TEARDOWN across three consecutive runs — verdict flipped RENOVATION->TEARDOWN, locking downstream.

DECISIVE 2026-06-03: THREE runs on essentially-equivalent content scored 12/14 RENOVATION, 10/14 TEARDOWN, then 9/14 TEARDOWN (P2+P3 FAIL) — verdict moved the WRONG way as the site improved. The 9/14 run is SELF-CONTRADICTORY: it evidenced icp_buyer_title as 'Agency Owner / Principal' yet failed PRE-HARD P2 claiming 'no named distributor archetype' — the same run both found and denied the archetype. Conclusion: the gate is too non-deterministic to FUNCTION as a gate. Variance reduction is GATE-BREAKING priority.

attempts.what: treated the earlier P3 fail as a fixed mis-rule ('P3 miscalibrated for distributor model')
attempts.result: partial
attempts.reason: it is not a deterministic wrong rule — a later run passed P3 on the identical product. The real issue is VARIANCE: the survey was an LLM judgment that landed differently across runs.

attempts.what: REMOVED the model from the survey entirely (2026-06-03)
attempts.result: success
attempts.reason: Reframed per 'generator owns invariants': the build PLANTS machine-checkable data-* markers from the card (markerProps, throws on generic/off-enum at build time); the survey GREPS them and DERIVES the verdict (P2/P3 derived from the field results, never re-judged). No model in the path. PROVEN: 3 identical runs -> TEARDOWN/TEARDOWN/TEARDOWN.

solution.approach: The survey is now a deterministic DOM-marker grep with no LLM. Build plants markers via markerProps (cais-build-template-v2/lib/surveyMarkers.ts) from the card; survey route fetches survey-manifest.json -> fetches each route's DOM -> deriveSurveyFromDom (survey-markers.ts) -> loadCardSurvey -> survey.ts. P2/P3 derived from field results (P2 IS the distributor field check) so they cannot self-contradict. Coherence enforced upstream by the build throw, not by a survey judgment. The OpenCode survey workflow (survey.yml) + SURVEY_MODE.md retired; the cockpit kickoff proxies to the deterministic route.
solution.key_change: RESOLVED 2026-06-03. Deterministic marker grep replaces LLM survey. Same input -> same verdict (proven 3x TEARDOWN). RENOVATION-determinism pending one design-build run that replants markers with named values.

entries.product: shared / any Next.js + @supabase/ssr middleware (the pattern ported from Corporate-AI-Solutions)
entries.error_pattern: Authenticated user is bounced to login when REFRESHING an authed page — session lost on refresh, intermittent (hits when the access token needs re-issuing)
error_symptoms: Refreshing an authed page redirects to /login (or /admin/login) despite being signed in
Session "randomly" drops after some idle time + a refresh; fine right after login
@supabase/ssr middleware using the per-cookie get/set/remove callbacks (not getAll/setAll)
Cookies sb-<ref>-auth-token.0/.1 present but partial/corrupt after a refresh

solution.approach: The middleware cookie set()/remove() callbacks reassign `response = NextResponse.next(...)` on EVERY call, discarding cookies set by prior calls. Supabase chunks the auth token across multiple cookies (…-auth-token.0/.1 + refresh); on a token refresh getUser() writes several cookies but only the LAST survives on the response → the browser gets a partial/corrupt session cookie → the next server render getUser() fails → redirect to login.
solution.answer: Create `response` ONCE; in set()/remove() write to that SAME response (response.cookies.set / request.cookies.set) and do NOT recreate it. On @supabase/ssr >=0.5 prefer the getAll/setAll pattern (writes all cookies on one response). Detection: grep middleware.ts for `response = NextResponse.next` appearing inside the cookie set/remove callbacks (count 2-3 with the get/set/remove pattern).

attempts.tried: Added @caistech/report-generator to serverComponentsExternalPackages alongside @react-pdf/renderer (to keep native deps out of the bundle)
attempts.result: Made it WORSE — Node's native ESM loader then resolves the package and rejects the extensionless './render' import (ESM fullySpecified)

entries.error_pattern: Branded PDF shows literal HTML entities (' for apostrophe, & for &), drops/mis-renders non-Latin1 glyphs (arrow -> shows as stray quote/blank), and orphans list bullets (lone bullet at page bottom, its text on the next page)
error_symptoms: every apostrophe/quote in the PDF body renders as the literal string '
ampersands render as &
unicode arrows (U+2192) render as a stray quote or blank — em-dash and bullet render fine (they are WinAnsi)
a bullet appears at the bottom of a page with its text pushed to the top of the next page

attempts.tried: Assumed the analysis TEXT stored in the DB was HTML-escaped
attempts.result: No — the DB holds clean text and the on-screen (browser) rendering is fine; the escaping is introduced by the PDF renderer

solution.approach: The package's Markdown component fed marked.lexer's token.text (which marked HTML-ESCAPES: ' -> ', & -> &) straight into react-pdf <Text>, which renders the literal string (react-pdf does NOT decode HTML entities). react-pdf's built-in Helvetica is WinAnsi-only so glyphs like the arrow drop. And list items were plain Views that split across page breaks. Fix is IN THE PACKAGE (v0.1.1): cleanText() decodes marked's named+numeric entities and swaps out-of-WinAnsi glyphs (arrows/smart-quotes/ellipsis) to ASCII (leave dashes + bullet), applied at every leaf text node; wrap={false} on the list-item View.
solution.answer: Published @caistech/report-generator@0.1.1 (cleanText + wrap=false); consumers bump to >=0.1.1. Verified against the exact failing strings.

entries.product: Kira (4 rounds) + @caistech/elevenlabs-convai — pattern applies to EVERY convai memory consumer
entries.error_pattern: Voice agent does not remember a prior conversation. User briefs the agent at length, reconnects, and it has no recall ("I don't have access to past conversations" / greets on a stale objective). Memory was "fixed" 4+ separate times over 6 months and stayed broken each time.
error_symptoms: agent greets with a stale/first-ever objective instead of recent context
agent says it cannot access past conversations despite a wired memory loop
kira_memory / memory table is empty or only holds seed rows
no error anywhere — tool webhooks 200 or are simply never called; the failure is SILENT in every layer
each fix round's commit message independently asserts "memory never actually worked"

attempts.tried: Bind the post-call webhook (2026-05-25) — per-agent platform_settings.webhook → workspace-scoped bindWorkspaceWebhook
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 1. Memory still broken — link 4 was also broken.

attempts.tried: Remove hardcoded webhook-secret fallback + adopt hub HMAC verifier (2026-05-25)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 2. Memory still broken.

attempts.tried: Correct tool-router auth to header-secret, not post-call HMAC (2026-05-25)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 4. Memory still broken — link 7 was broken.

attempts.tried: Adopt the canonical @caistech/elevenlabs-convai loop wholesale (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Correct architecture. Memory still broken — links 6 and 7 broken.

attempts.tried: Fix get_conversation_context status filter — "welcome-back recall never fired" (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 7. Memory still broken — link 6 (distil) was broken.

attempts.tried: Wire post-call distillation — "kira_memory was never filling" (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Correct fix for link 6. Memory still broken — link 5 (agent never CALLS the tool) was broken.

attempts.tried: Create the kira_logs table its writers assumed (2026-07-20)
attempts.result: Removed a silent-fail residual that had been HIDING the breaks above.

solution.approach: The loop is a CHAIN of 7 independent links, and a break in ANY one produces the identical, silent "agent has no memory" symptom: (1) post-call webhook bound at workspace scope; (2) post-call HMAC verifies; (3) memory tools ATTACHED to the agent (tool_ids); (4) tool-webhook auth header matches (re-provision required whenever the secret changes); (5) the agent MODEL actually emits the tool call; (6) post-call distil writes durable memory rows; (7) recall reads them back with the right filters. Every round above correctly fixed one link while another was still broken, so each fix was real AND the system stayed broken. The root cause of the RECURRENCE is not any single link — it is that no test ever exercised the whole chain (talk → disconnect → reconnect → assert recall), so "fixed" was always inferred from code, never observed from behaviour.
solution.answer: Do not debug links individually. Add ONE end-to-end behavioural test as the definition of done: hold a real conversation, disconnect, reconnect, assert the agent names a specific fact from the prior call. Run it in CI against prod. Any of the 4 rounds above would have failed it on day one. Treat a green unit/route test as evidence of NOTHING for this subsystem.
solution.code_path: kira: lib/kira/convai.ts (loop mount), app/api/kira/create/route.ts (provisioning), app/api/kira/webhooks/* (7 routes), scripts/reprovision-kira-agents.mjs. hub: @caistech/elevenlabs-convai createConvaiWebhookRoutes / createConversationTools / distillConversationToMemory.

entries.product: Kira — applies to any repo that hardcodes the agent LLM instead of taking DEFAULT_AGENT_LLM
entries.error_pattern: Voice agent with a correctly-wired memory loop still never remembers, because the agent MODEL silently stops emitting tool calls. Every route, table, secret and webhook is correct; the tools are simply never invoked.
error_symptoms: memory tables stay empty but no route ever 4xx/5xx — because no request arrives
recall works in a short test call and degrades as the conversation lengthens
agent verbally claims it cannot access memory/documents rather than erroring
the repo pins a recent @caistech/elevenlabs-convai yet passes its own `llm:` value

attempts.tried: Audited webhook binding, HMAC, tool attachment, tool auth header, table columns, RLS
attempts.result: All correct — the wiring was not the fault.

solution.approach: @caistech/elevenlabs-convai sets DEFAULT_AGENT_LLM = gpt-4.1-mini (v0.4.2, commit c408d98) SPECIFICALLY because gpt-4o-mini drops tool calls over long conversations. Kira provisions agents through a raw ElevenLabs POST that hardcodes `llm: gpt-4o-mini`, bypassing the hub default entirely — so the one repo that mounted the full loop correctly overrode the one setting that makes it fire. Memory that is never CALLED is indistinguishable from memory that does not exist.
solution.answer: Never hardcode the agent LLM. Take DEFAULT_AGENT_LLM from the hub package, or route provisioning through the hub createAgent(). When auditing a "memory does not work" report, check the MODEL before the plumbing — it is the cheapest check and it produces zero error signal.

error_symptoms: package.json shows the dependency in N repos — used as the rollout evidence
the behaviour fails in a repo everyone believed was covered
no repo-level check distinguishes "imports the package" from "mounts its routes"
version drift across consumers goes unnoticed (0.1.6 → 0.5.0 in the same portfolio)

attempts.result: FALSE POSITIVE — proves installation, not integration. This is the check that produced the overclaim.

entries.product: Kira — class applies to every prompted agent across the portfolio
entries.error_pattern: The system prompt lists tools the agent does not have. The agent, behaving correctly, tells the user it "cannot access" the capability — which reads to the user as a broken product rather than an unbuilt one. The upstream half of the feature (ingestion/UI) ships and the retrieval half never does.
error_symptoms: agent says "I can't access that document" / "I can't access URLs" for a documented feature
an upload UI and ingest route exist and write rows successfully
no retrieval route exists for the agent to call — the store is write-only
the prompt enumerates the tool by name, so the agent believes it should work

attempts.tried: Attaching the named tools to close the gap

It stops being exercised, so it silently rots — and then fires on a rare trigger (first real payment, first invite, first import) and mints a broken resource nobody is looking for.

the stale path is never hit in testing because its trigger is rare (a real paid checkout)

solution.approach: Kira's Stripe webhook carried its own createElevenLabsAgent() frozen at Jan-2026: no memory tools attached (zero memory loop), no llm pinned, the deprecated platform_settings.webhook shape ElevenLabs silently ignores, a hardcoded `|| 'kira-webhook-secret'` fallback, no origin allowlist, a 4th copy of the system prompt, and it wrote kira_agents.name where canonical writes agent_name. Here the webhook had no business minting agents at all: accounts belong to /api/onboarding/complete (which creates a real confirmed auth.users and lets the trigger link the app row) and agents belong to /api/kira/create (the only path that attaches tools + continuity prompt + allowlist + post-call webhook). entries.error_pattern: Voice-agent memory tool routes (recall_memory/save_memory/start_conversation) accept unauthenticated POSTs. Where start_conversation is NOT session-gated, a public agent id (readable from the client bundle) mints a conversation bound to the agent owner, and recall then returns that owner's memory — a cross-tenant read/write.
error_symptoms: tool webhook request_headers is Content-Type only — no shared-secret or HMAC
start_conversation returns 200 "Agent not found" for a synthetic agent id (no session gate) instead of 401
recall_memory / save_memory return 200 and derive identity from conversation_id with no auth
the agent id is NEXT_PUBLIC / present in the client bundle

attempts.result: Established: singify start has no session gate (exposed); prelabz + sayfix return 401 Unauthorized session (gated at the door); all three leave recall/save unauthenticated

solution.approach: Two-tier reality: repos that session-gate start_conversation (prelabz, sayfix) are protected because the identity-binding conversation row can only be created by a verified session; a repo that does NOT session-gate it (singify) is exposed via the public agent id — the same hole Kira had. Until then, patch each exposed repo workspace tools in place with the header (scripts/patch-tool-secret-headers.mjs pattern) AND ensure start_conversation is session-gated. attempts.tried: Assumed the audit write succeeded because the helper is awaited and the route returned 200
attempts.result: FAILED — the helper swallows insert errors with console.error only, so the caller cannot distinguish success from failure

entries.error_symptoms: Tasks are in the database and on NO page. /admin/asked-for looks calm, the approval flow finds nothing, the owner is told his email was drafted and it never sends. Rows have handled_by='orchestrator' and a non-terminal status. Nothing errors; no log line; the row looks healthy in the table. Only rows older than the 15-minute grace window are affected, which makes it look like a dispatch bug when the dispatch was fine.

attempts.tried: Inspected the dispatch-time writer (lib/kira/swarm/tool-handlers.ts mirrorTask, status: result.status) and the wire adapter (orchestrator-adapter.ts) and the orchestrator's own /v1/dispatch route
attempts.result: FAILED to explain it - all three are correct on disk. Led to a false 'the deployed build must differ from main' theory. It did not; deployed == origin/main.

attempts.tried: Compared deployed Vercel production against origin/main HEAD
attempts.result: Ruled out deploy drift - no unpushed commits, latest prod deploy is the current HEAD

attempts.tried: Grepped for EVERY writer of the table rather than the obvious two
attempts.result: SUCCESS - found a third writer nobody had checked: the reconcile cron

solution.approach: app/api/cron/reconcile-tasks/route.ts called coordinator.getTaskState(), which returns a TaskStatus OBJECT, then wrote `status: live` (the object) instead of `live.status`. The guard hid it: `live === task.status` compares an object to a string, so it is NEVER equal, every row looked changed, and every 20-minute run rewrote the same damage. Fix: read live.status, validate it with a new runtime validator asTaskState() (a bare `x as TaskState` cast validates nothing and is what let an object through), skip the row when unreadable, and add a CHECK constraint on kira_tasks.status so the write errors instead of persisting. GENERAL LESSON: when a column holds a serialised object, enumerate EVERY writer of that table - the culprit is the one nobody thought was a writer - and never trust an equality guard that compares across types.

attempts.tried: Suspected the domain lost verification (the message says so, and a prior SayFix fix had exactly that cause) — checked SPF/DKIM/MX for updates.corporateaisolutions.com via DNS
attempts.result: WRONG PATH. All records present and correct (SPF include:amazonses.com, resend._domainkey DKIM, feedback-smtp MX in ap-northeast-1). The 550 does not mean DNS is broken.

attempts.tried: Suspected the admin allowlist or the auth_user_id link broke in the Seoul->Sydney migration — joined public.admin_users to auth.users
attempts.result: Ruled out. uwe@factory2key.com.au is super_admin, linked to a confirmed auth user with a password, last sign-in 2026-06-30.

attempts.tried: Suspected middleware / callback drift or a stale production deploy — reviewed src/middleware.ts, /api/auth/callback (PKCE) and /api/auth/confirm (token_hash), and compared the deployed commit SHA to origin/main
attempts.result: Ruled out. Minted a magiclink token_hash with admin/generate_link and walked it through /api/auth/confirm on production: 307 -> /admin, session cookie set, /admin rendered. Every code path works; only DELIVERY was broken.

attempts.tried: Read Supabase auth_logs (Management API analytics/endpoints/logs.all) for the failing request id
attempts.result: FOUND IT. The 550 came from Resend at send time, meaning the SMTP credential authenticated but its account has no verified sending domain.

attempts.tried: Compared the Vercel RESEND_API_KEY updatedAt to the last successful app email and the last successful admin login
attempts.result: CONFIRMED. RESEND_API_KEY was rotated in Vercel 2026-06-29 11:50 UTC to a key from a different Resend account (the mcmdennis org). Supabase Auth's own smtp_pass copy was never updated, so it kept the OLD account's key. All auth email dead from 2026-06-29; unnoticed for a month because password login still worked.

solution.approach: Supabase Auth stores its OWN copy of the Resend API key in smtp_pass, independent of the app's Vercel RESEND_API_KEY. Rotating the app's key does not update Supabase's, and nothing surfaces the divergence. THE DISCRIMINATOR for the identical 550/400 'domain is not verified' message: call GET https://api.resend.com/domains with THAT SPECIFIC KEY. If the domain is absent, the key is from the wrong Resend account (this bug — fix the key). If it is present but status != verified, verification genuinely lapsed (fix DNS — the earlier SayFix case). Do not start with DNS. Fix: PATCH https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/{ref}/config/auth {smtp_pass: <current key>} with the management token from ~/.supabase-token, then PROVE it by POSTing /auth/v1/otp and confirming a 200 plus a delivered status in the Resend API — a saved config is not a working send.
solution.code_path: scripts/repair-auth-smtp.mjs (f2k-projects) — reads RESEND_API_KEY from .env.local without printing it, refuses to push a key whose account lacks the verified domain, PATCHes Supabase Auth, then verifies with a real send. Diagnosis path: GET /v1/projects/{ref}/analytics/endpoints/logs.all?sql=select ... from auth_logs — the only place the underlying SMTP error is visible; the client only ever sees a generic 500.

entries.error_pattern: Browser shows "Unexpected token 'R', "Request En"... is not valid JSON" when uploading a file through a Next.js API route on Vercel
entries.error_symptoms: A user cannot upload a real file; small test files work; nothing lands in Supabase Storage OR the DB (so it is not an RLS or insert problem); no POST appears in Vercel runtime logs; every row that ever succeeded is small (here, all under 1.1MB against a bucket configured for 50MB). The error names the word "Request" because that is the first token of Vercel's plain-text body.

attempts.tried: Audited Supabase storage RLS policies, bucket allowed_mime_types and file_size_limit
attempts.result: all correct — not the cause

attempts.tried: Searched Vercel runtime logs for the failing request
attempts.result: no POST present; retention is ~24h. The ABSENCE of the request is the diagnostic — the body never reached the function

attempts.tried: Probed the deployed endpoint unauthenticated at increasing body sizes
attempts.result: WORKED — 1MB and 4MB returned 401 JSON (function reached); 4.6MB returned 413 FUNCTION_PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE (edge rejected). No writes needed to find the ceiling.

solution.approach: Two defects. (1) Vercel rejects request bodies over 4.5MB at the EDGE, before the function runs, with a plain-text "Request Entity Too Large". Any file posted through a route handler is therefore capped at 4.5MB regardless of what the storage bucket allows. Fix: have the BROWSER upload straight to Supabase Storage via createSignedUploadUrl/uploadToSignedUrl and send only JSON metadata through the function; keep ownership by scoping the signed key to {user.id}/ and re-checking the prefix server-side. (2) The client called await response.json() BEFORE checking response.ok, so a non-JSON error body surfaced as a parser complaint instead of a usable message — always read errors with a text-first helper.

entries.generalises_to: EVERY repo that posts a file through a Next.js route handler on Vercel. Check for formData.get("file") in app/api/**. The same probe (unauthenticated POST at 4MB then 4.6MB) identifies it in minutes without touching data.

entries.error_pattern: ACCOUNT TAKEOVER: a post-payment "complete onboarding" endpoint sets a password (or otherwise mutates an account) using the email address taken from the checkout session, which the payer typed and which was never verified as theirs
entries.error_symptoms: Nothing looks wrong — the takeover is indistinguishable from a completed purchase: a real payment, a working signup. The victim notices only when their own password stops working. Found by walking the paid path end-to-end for the first time, not by reading code — no scanner flags it because every individual call is legitimate.

attempts.tried: Read the endpoint looking for a missing auth check
attempts.result: There is no missing check — the endpoint is unauthenticated BY DESIGN, because the payer has no session yet. The flaw is what it does with an identity it cannot prove.

attempts.tried: Considered validating the email against the Stripe customer
attempts.result: Does not help. Checkout lets anyone type any address and must, because people pay on behalf of others every day. The endpoint cannot obtain proof of identity from the session.

attempts.tried: Ran the exploit against our own account with the old code
attempts.result: CONFIRMED: real password works=false, attacker password works=true. Reproduced, then restored.

solution.approach: An existing account has NOTHING mutated — not the password, and deliberately not the rest either: the valuation upsert is keyed on user_id with onConflict so an unverified caller would overwrite a real owner's baseline, and writing the subscription id would detach the subscription they are actually paying for. Return {ok:true, existing:true}, log a warning carrying the session id, and send the payer to sign in, where forgot-password proves ownership by email — which is exactly the proof the endpoint cannot obtain and must not fake. Also drop any listUsers() paging that only existed to serve the removed write.

entries.generalises_to: Any endpoint that acts on an identity asserted by an untrusted caller. The fix is never better validation of the assertion — it is refusing to mutate anything for an identity you cannot prove, and routing the caller to a channel that can prove it.

attempts.result: All correct. Reachability was never the problem.

Self-selects for exactly the low-commitment visitor the fallback exists to serve, and those people do not report it.

attempts.tried: Checked once that the fallback renders
attempts.result: It did. A single run passes about a third of the time against this defect.

attempts.tried: Assumed the tester was mis-testing
attempts.result: Wrong. Identical code genuinely behaves differently per connection outcome.

attempts.result: Rejected — the fallback REPLACES the voice UI, so firing early steals a slow-but-working connection from someone who does have a mic. That is the opposite failure and a worse one.

attempts.tried: Read the route and confirmed verification exists
attempts.result: It does exist. It is conditional, which is the defect.

attempts.tried: Assumed the secret would always be set

attempts.tried: Deleted the webhook to rotate it
attempts.result: 405 webhook_in_use — must unbind, delete, create, re-bind, in that order.

entries.generalises_to: Every `if (secret)` around a verification step is a fail-open. Absent config must refuse, never skip — a check that quietly does nothing is indistinguishable from one that passed.

attempts.result: The handler is fine and was never reached.

entries.product: Any Next.js app with auth middleware — class applies to every published marketing page
entries.error_pattern: A public page is not added to the middleware allowlist, so every visitor without a session is 307d to /login — and the whole verification stack goes green over it
entries.error_symptoms: curl -L FOLLOWS the redirect and returns 200. The deploy gate's app-marker assertion MATCHES, because the login page carries the product name too. deploy-status PASSES, correctly, because production genuinely is serving the expected SHA. Three checks, all correct, all passing over a page nobody can open. Customer-visible.

attempts.tried: curl -L and asserting 200
attempts.result: Passes. Following the redirect is precisely what hides the bug.

attempts.tried: Asserting the product name appears in the HTML
attempts.result: Passes — the login page carries it.

attempts.tried: Matching the words "sign in" in the body
attempts.result: Rejected — a marketing page routinely LINKS to sign-in. Match a type="password" input instead: a marketing page should never contain one.

solution.approach: redirect: "manual" is the whole check. Mark a page @public-route, probe without following redirects, FAIL on any 3xx naming the status AND the Location ("307 -> /login" is a diagnosis, "307" is not), and WARN on a 200 whose body contains a password input. FAILS when routes are marked but no base URL is configured, because an unverified public page is the bug itself.

entries.generalises_to: If your check follows the thing that went wrong, it will never see it go wrong.

entries.product: Any Vercel-deployed product — one month of silent failure before detection
entries.error_pattern: Every production deploy fails at npm install (expired NODE_AUTH_TOKEN -> 401 from GitHub Packages) while production keeps serving the last successful build
entries.error_symptoms: Undetectable by any reachability check: the site answers 200 all day, nothing is down, no alert fires. Discovered only when work known to have been merged turned up missing. The undeployed commits included RLS hardening and admin MFA enforcement — security work already described to a partner as remediated.

attempts.tried: Assumed the fix had been reverted or had not worked
attempts.result: Neither. It was merged and correct, and had never been deployed.

attempts.tried: Health-checking the public URL
attempts.result: Passes. A stale production is a HEALTHY production — that is the trap.

attempts.tried: Checking that the URL returns 200
attempts.result: Vercel's SSO deployment-protection page ALSO returns 200 with a login screen, so this passes against a product nobody can reach.

solution.approach: Assert three things: the latest production deployment is READY; its COMMIT SHA matches the expected ref (the assertion that catches a stale production); and the public URL serves the app, not a protection wall (an app-specific marker in the HTML). Missing config FAILS rather than skips, because every product deploys — a genuinely non-Vercel repo opts out with a recorded reason. Runs on push AND on a daily cron so token expiry is caught without a push.

entries.generalises_to: Before trusting ANY live test, prove production is running the code you think it is. A passing test against a stale build is worse than no test — it manufactures false confidence.

entries.error_pattern: renderToBuffer produces a PDF that pdf-parse rejects with "bad XRef entry" on Linux CI, while passing 11/11 locally on Windows + Node 24
entries.error_symptoms: A malformed cross-reference table — the artifact is broken, not merely different. Matters more than a flaky test suggests: producing valid PDFs is this package's entire job, and a common runtime produces invalid ones. Surfaced by the first CI run this repo has ever had.

attempts.tried: Version drift between local and CI
attempts.result: RULED OUT — the lock pins @react-pdf/renderer 4.5.1 and pdf-parse 1.1.4, and both resolve to exactly that locally.

attempts.tried: Read-before-flush race
attempts.result: RULED OUT — renderToBuffer is awaited.

attempts.tried: Raised CI from Node 20 to Node 24 to match local
attempts.result: Eliminated the runtime as a candidate AND the failure grew from one test to at least three. Platform is now the remaining candidate; nothing further is established.

solution.approach: NOT SOLVED. The whole suite is describe.skip-ped when CI is set — deliberately keyed on CI rather than on platform, which would assert an undemonstrated cause, and scoped to the whole suite because the measured blast radius is 3+ tests rather than the one that happened to go red first. Stays visible as a SKIP rather than vanishing.

entries.generalises_to: Record what has been RULED OUT, not only what was tried. An open entry with three eliminated hypotheses is worth more to the next person than a closed one with a guess.

entries.product: cais-shared-services / @caistech/report-generator (any repo parsing PDFs in tests)
entries.error_pattern: UnknownErrorException: bad XRef entry (also "Illegal character: 41", "Ignoring invalid character 255 in hex string") from pdf-parse
error_symptoms: PDF assertions pass locally but fail in Linux CI
the same suite fails a DIFFERENT number of tests between runs / Node versions
near-identical documents disagree ("omits watermark" passes, "includes watermark" fails)
looks exactly like a corrupt generated artifact, and every check that goes through the parser agrees

attempts.tried: Blame version drift; pin @react-pdf/renderer + pdf-parse via the lockfile
attempts.result: FAILED — CI and local already resolved identical trees

attempts.tried: Blame a read-before-flush race inside renderPdf
attempts.result: FAILED — renderToBuffer is awaited

attempts.tried: Blame the Node version; raise CI from Node 20 to 24
attempts.result: FAILED and MISLEADING — failures grew 1 -> 3+, which read as "the runtime modulates the damage" and pointed at the platform. It was just a different draw from a non-deterministic parser.

attempts.tried: Conclude the platform, and skip the whole suite when CI is set
attempts.result: WRONG DIAGNOSIS — the renderer was never at fault. Cost six days of a package that could not verify its own output.

attempts.tried: Blame concurrency between parallel renders (module-level state in @react-pdf)
attempts.result: FAILED — 260 renders up to 32-way parallel were byte-identical

attempts.tried: Blame a platform newline (os.EOL would give Linux 19-byte xref entries)
attempts.result: FAILED — no os.EOL in @react-pdf; _write appends a hardcoded newline

solution.approach: THE TRAP: every check ran THROUGH pdf-parse, and a broken PARSER and a broken ARTIFACT come back red identically — so no amount of that evidence can separate them. You must measure without the suspect. Two checks did it: (1) a STRUCTURAL sweep asserting the invariant pdf.js itself enforces (every in-use xref offset points at "<num> <gen> obj"), through no parser at all — 57/57 clean on Linux, byte-for-byte the same sizes as Windows; (2) a CROSS-PARSE of a committed WINDOWS-generated PDF that Windows pdf-parse accepts — Linux pdf-parse threw bad XRef entry on IDENTICAL bytes, and identical bytes cannot be corrupt on one OS. Root cause: pdf-parse@1.1.4 bundles pdf.js v1.10.100 (2018) and rejects structurally-valid PDFs inconsistently. Fix: replace pdf-parse with unpdf (the portfolio parser, already in DealFindrs) and un-skip the suite. GENERALISES: whenever a tool is both the measuring instrument and a suspect, find one measurement that does not use it.

entries.error_pattern: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "<field>") thrown from INSIDE a library, on a path TypeScript says is impossible
error_symptoms: a required-in-the-type argument is omitted and the library throws a bare TypeError instead of a named error
tsc is clean, the build is clean, the tests are clean — and the path is still broken for JS callers
only reproduces from plain JS, or from a caller that cast/spread its options

attempts.tried: Trust the type signature — the field is required, so it cannot be undefined
attempts.result: FALSE for every JS consumer, every "as any" cast, every object built by spread or parsed from JSON. The type is a compile-time claim about SOME callers, not a runtime guarantee about all of them.

attempts.tried: Fix only the field that was reported
attempts.result: INCOMPLETE — the same omission existed on every sibling validator and on the options object itself

solution.approach: Two rules. (1) VALIDATE THE SHAPE AT THE PUBLIC BOUNDARY, not just the fields: check the section object exists before reading fields off it, so a missing section names itself instead of throwing from library internals. Note the asymmetry that makes this worth fixing — a missing FIELD gave a clear "x.y is required" while a missing SECTION gave a bare TypeError, so the caller who made the LARGER mistake was told LESS. (2) Check PRESENCE, not truthiness, for anything where empty is legal (an empty markdown body is a valid document; rejecting "" is a regression dressed as validation). GENERALISES: a published package meets callers tsc never sees. The same blind spot produced 0.1.2 (dist/ unimportable from Node ESM — invisible because the tests imported src/ through vitest resolver) and 0.1.3 (this). If a defect can only be found by CALLING the package the way a consumer does, no type check or build will ever find it.

entries.error_pattern: A validation or drift guard written as Math.abs(a - b) > threshold reports NO PROBLEM when the value is NaN, because every comparison with NaN is false
error_symptoms: the guard logs nothing, throws nothing, and the bad value is written anyway
the visible symptom is generic and far downstream — "the number never moves", a blank figure, a null column
the guard has tests, and they all pass, because they only ever feed it well-formed input

attempts.tried: Write the drift check the obvious way: Math.abs(recomputed - stored) > 0.005
attempts.result: FAILED SILENTLY. A malformed inputs row made computeValuation return NaN; the comparison was false, the guard concluded "no drift", and NaN was written to the column.

attempts.tried: Feed the function inputs of the WRONG SHAPE in a test, rather than only wrong-but-valid ones
attempts.result: WORKED — surfaced immediately as baseline NaN and reason undefined, exposing both the bad input and the guard that could not fire on it.

solution.approach: Assert Number.isFinite() on the computed value BEFORE any comparison, and refuse. Keep the malformed input as a permanent fixture. THE GENERAL RULE: a guard built on a numeric comparison must be proven to FIRE on the worst input, not merely on a plausible wrong one — otherwise the first thing it meets in production is the one case it cannot detect.

entries.error_pattern: A Supabase .select() names a column that lives on a DIFFERENT table; tsc is clean because the client is untyped, and it errors only when the code actually runs
error_symptoms: typecheck, build and unit tests are all green
the feature simply does nothing in production — no crash the user sees, just a value that never appears
the error is inside a caught block and surfaces, if at all, as a log line nobody reads

attempts.tried: Select model_version from business_valuations because a sibling concept lived nearby
attempts.result: WRONG — model_version is on valuation_snapshots (the append-only history), never on the current row. Would have surfaced as "readiness_now never gets written".

attempts.tried: Grep the migrations for the column before trusting the select
attempts.result: WORKED, and took ten seconds. grep -rn "model_version" supabase/migrations/ named the owning table immediately.

solution.approach: Before selecting a column you have not personally seen on that table, grep the migrations for it. An untyped client turns a schema mistake into a runtime-only failure, and the runtime symptom is almost always the vague one ("it never updates") rather than an error naming the column.

entries.error_pattern: RuntimeError: supabaseKey is required (createClient at module evaluation in a file imported by a 'use client' component)
error_symptoms: browser crashes with supabaseKey is required from a client component
build passes but dev runtime blows up because SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is empty string in the client bundle
only NEXT_PUBLIC_* env vars are inlined into client bundles; any other process.env.X is undefined there

solution.approach: Split the module: a client-safe config file (used by the widget) vs a server-only module (import "server-only") that constructs the service-role Supabase client at module scope. Move side-effectful client construction (createClient) into the server-only half; let async callbacks dynamically import() the supabase client so only the server path executes it.

entries.error_pattern: Unexpected end of JSON input on res.json() after POST /api/onboarding/discovery/session
error_symptoms: client fetch to a route handler that throws (unhandled) gets an empty/HTML 500 body
startSession() throws because deps.existingAgentId is required but never passed (agent IS provisioned, ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID is set in env)
route returned NextResponse.json only on success; the throw produced a body that res.json() cannot parse

solution.approach: 1) Wire the provisioned agent id into the discovery deps: existingAgentId: process.env.ELEVENLABS_AGENT_ID || undefined. 2) Wrap startSession in try/catch returning NextResponse.json({error}, {status:500}). 3) Client: check res.ok before .json(), surface error.message instead of crashing.

entries.error_pattern: useState only works in Client Components. Add the "use client" directive at the top of the file
error_symptoms: Runtime TypeError: react-client-hook-in-server-component
A marketing component (Nav.tsx) uses React.useState/useEffect without a 'use client' directive
error surfaces at the server layout that mounts the component (MktShell -> MarketingLayout)

attempts.tried: Full-scan sibling marketing components (MktMobileMenu, SpecProvider) for the same missing directive
attempts.result: Both had "use client"; only Nav.tsx had lost it during a styling port

solution.approach: Any component using client hooks and rendered by a server layout must declare "use client" as the first line. When porting/restyling server-rendered marketing components, keep the directive.
solution.answer: Prepend "use client"; to Nav.tsx (first line, before imports). Verified with next build (compiled successfully).

entries.error_pattern: beta tester stuck at "Loading your onboarding session…" spinner on /plan; page never advances
error_symptoms: Spinner on /plan with Loader2 renders indefinitely, no error message
No GET /api/identity/plan request fires at all (initialBetaCode stuck null)
GET /api/identity/plan request stays pending forever (no client timeout)
Happens when tester reaches /plan with no code in URL AND empty sessionStorage

attempts.result: Confirmed two independent hang paths, both surfaced as the same spinner
attempts.tried: Traced loading gate on /plan -> identityLoading only cleared on settle/reject, never in-flight

attempts.result: Code preserved correctly; not the loss point
attempts.tried: Checked magic-link redirect leg (BetaRedeem -> /auth/callback -> /plan?code=...)

solution.answer: A null initialBetaCode was the only value the canonical identity load bailed on, and previously no-code arrivals left it at null forever -> permanent spinner. Empty string (already used as the cleared sentinel in continueMismatch) is the fix for the no-code path.
solution.approach: Two fixes in app/plan/page.tsx. (1) URL-read effect now ALWAYS sets initialBetaCode (empty string when no code found) so null means only "URL not yet read" and a code-less arrival proceeds instead of stalling the identity effect which bails on null. (2) Identity fetch now uses AbortController with a 15s timeout that aborts into the error path with a friendly message, plus abort on unmount and timer cleanup.

entries.error_pattern: User clicks the signup/magic-link email and lands on the login page with 'Missing verification code' (no session).
error_symptoms: Email link points at https://<ref>.supabase.co/auth/v1/verify?token=...&type=signup&redirect_to=... (the default {{ .ConfirmationURL }} shape), NOT at the app's /auth/callback
App is redirected to /login?error=Missing+verification+code
email IS confirmed in auth.users (email_confirmed_at is set) - only the session hand-off failed
Affects EVERY self-service email flow (signup, magiclink, recovery); invites are unaffected because they are sent via admin.generateLink + Resend in token_hash form
Only reproduces when the email was issued by an implicit-flow client (flowType: 'implicit'); a PKCE issuer would instead yield ?code=

attempts.tried: Re-reading /auth/callback expecting it to read the session from the redirect
attempts.result: It only handles ?code= (exchangeCodeForSession) and ?token_hash=&type= (verifyOtp); it cannot see the access_token because it arrives in the URL fragment (#access_token=...), which browsers never send to the server

attempts.tried: Reading/patching the hosted email templates via the Supabase Management API (api.supabase.com/v1/projects/<ref>/config/auth)
attempts.result: 401 'Your account does not have the necessary privileges to access this endpoint' - token lacks privilege; templates are dashboard-only for this project

attempts.tried: Using the new sb_secret_ service-role key against the auth admin REST API from PowerShell/Invoke-RestMethod
attempts.result: 401 'Forbidden use of secret API key in browser' - fixed by sending an explicit non-browser User-Agent header (e.g. 'curl/8.4.0'); the key is fine, the UA was the trigger

solution.approach: Root cause = mismatch between the email-issuing client's flow and the email template shape. LingoPure's createOtpIssuerClient() sets flowType: 'implicit', so GoTrue's /auth/v1/verify returns the session in the URL fragment, which the server-side /auth/callback can never read. A fragment-consistent design MUST use the self-contained token_hash template form (which verifyOtp exchanges with no client-side state, so it works cross-device/browser/domain).
solution.answer: Set all five Supabase Auth email templates (Confirm signup, Magic link, Reset password, Invite, Change email) to the self-contained token_hash form: '{{ .SiteURL }}/auth/callback?token_hash={{ .TokenHash }}&type=<signup|magiclink|recovery|invite|email_change>&next=<path>'. Preconditions: auth.site_url = the public domain, that domain + /** in auth.additional_redirect_urls, and a callback that handles ?token_hash=&type=. Paste-ready branded bodies: docs/AUTH_EMAIL_TEMPLATES.md in lingopure. Do NOT use cais-shared-services/scripts/configure-email-templates.sh for this product - it still emits {{ .ConfirmationURL }} (PKCE-oriented) and reproduces the bug under an implicit issuer. Immediate user unblock while the templates are unfixed: sign in with email + password, because /verify already consumed the token and confirmed the email.

usage: Before fixing ANY bug, grep this file for matching error patterns. Also check SayFix DB for product-specific attempts.

Set both in Vercel (Production/Preview) AND ensure a live receiver verifies the same secret. Related: cas-pipeline-execute-dry-run-default.
